scope: Directed read-only review of nine-source delta, #91 shared seam, inherited WindowsJob/workflow/helper; original reviews retained separately

findings.title: Bind the policy loader to the actual trusted installed host
findings.description: The new module calls its PSScriptRoot parent a trusted installed host, but the unchanged native caller resolves and executes run_gonggong_config_agent.ps1 from the editable workspace textbox. That launcher dot-sources gonggong_runtime_policy.ps1 from the same workspace. Consequently both the policy code and its pinned-hash table are still selected by the workspace; changing that workspace/module can change the supposed safety root together with the policy. The actual caller does not use the running editor installedSourceRoot/verified host source. This is the previously identified trust-chain gap, not repaired merely by moving hashes from a workspace JSON lock into a workspace PowerShell file.
findings.minimal_correction: Resolve/launch the bootstrap and policy module from the running editor verified installed-host/source root (e.g. the existing GongGongHostPaths::engine_source route, after its normal trusted source checks); pass the editable workspace only as target data. Missing installed host provenance must fail closed for this model step. Retain pinned context/mandate and no-new-Agent semantics. Keep fixture installation and workspace separate so the test proves the actual production resolution rather than copying policy into a mutable workspace to mask the gap.
findings.validation_basis: Static actual-call-chain inspection; three native C++ hashes remained original. No Windows execution claim.

findings.title: Make the Windows runtime-source fixture match the actual launcher path
findings.description: The fixture copies config_agent into root/tools, but calls copy_runtime_policy only for installation. The current native setup caller runs root/tools/config_agent, which dot-sources root/tools/gonggong_runtime_policy.ps1. That module is never installed at that path. Therefore the Windows runtime-source path will fail before invoking the native selector and never reach the expected intake/resume. The reported successful mac native run has runtime_setup_and_resume=false and cannot cover this branch.
findings.minimal_correction: Fix the production trusted installed-host resolution in R49-G1-delta, then let this fixture execute the already populated installation/tools launcher. Do not just add the module to the mutable workspace as a substitute for establishing production trust. Run the exact runtime-source Windows simulation after the fix.
findings.validation_basis: Read-only AST/source destination check: the sole copy_runtime_policy call targets installation; root/tools launcher is explicitly copied, root/tools policy module is absent.

prior_findings.details: Native stdin now temporarily uses UTF8Encoding(false) and restores OutputEncoding/ErrorActionPreference in finally; plan/deployment/GitHub JSON reads explicitly use UTF8. Native fixture is a compiled PE, strictly decodes stdin UTF8, requires verified foundation/mandate markers and Chinese text, and writes BOMless UTF8 Unicode plan. Actual Windows execution remains required.

Actual verified full governance/core/template/foundation context and scoped inventory/operation mandate are assembled; forbidden exclusion language is removed, tools remain disabled, and metadata no longer claims independent framework registration. This is substantive context work, not mere renaming. The actual installed-host trust binding remains defective as R49-G1-delta describes.
